sources.note: Facts are short paraphrases for education, not medical advice. Each fact cites the chapter page that covers it. One entry covers both sides of a part.

Diaphragm.text: A dome-shaped sheet of muscle that separates the chest cavity from the abdominal cavity.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Diaphragm.text: It is the main muscle of breathing: it contracts and flattens to draw air into the lungs.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Rectus abdominis muscle.text: A paired muscle running down the front of the abdomen, covered by the rectus sheath.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Rectus abdominis muscle.text: It flexes the trunk, as when sitting up.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

External abdominal oblique muscle.text: The most superficial of the three layers of the side abdominal wall.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

External abdominal oblique muscle.text: It helps twist the trunk and bend it to the side.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.text: It forms the middle layer of the abdominal wall, beneath the external oblique.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Internal abdominal oblique muscle.text: It helps twist the trunk and bend it to the side.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Transversus abdominis muscle.text: The deepest layer of the abdominal wall, with fibres running across the abdomen.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Transversus abdominis muscle.text: It squeezes the abdomen during forceful breathing out, defecation, urination and childbirth.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

External intercostal muscles.text: Thin muscles between the ribs, on the sides of the chest.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

External intercostal muscles.text: They aid breathing in by raising the ribs.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Internal intercostal muscles.text: Muscles between the ribs, nearer the breastbone than the external intercostals.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Internal intercostal muscles.text: They help bring the ribs closer together in forced breathing out.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.4 Axial Muscles of the Abdominal Wall, and Thorax

Sternocleidomastoid muscle.text: A large neck muscle running from the breastbone and collarbone up to the skull behind the ear.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.3 Axial Muscles of the Head, Neck, and Back

Sternocleidomastoid muscle.text: It rotates and tilts the head, and tilts it forward when both sides act.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.3 Axial Muscles of the Head, Neck, and Back

Descending part of trapezius muscle.text: A broad muscle of the upper back, attached to the skull, spine, collarbone and shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Descending part of trapezius muscle.text: It raises the shoulders (shrugging) and pulls the shoulder blades together.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Latissimus dorsi muscle.text: A broad, triangular muscle on the lower part of the back.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Latissimus dorsi muscle.text: It is one of the muscles that move the arm downward at the shoulder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Rhomboid major muscle.text: A muscle between the spine and the shoulder blade, attached to vertebrae T2 to T5.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Rhomboid major muscle.text: It steadies the shoulder blade and pulls it toward the spine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Rhomboid minor muscle.text: A small muscle between the spine and the shoulder blade, attached to vertebrae C7 and T1.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Rhomboid minor muscle.text: It steadies the shoulder blade and pulls it toward the spine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Serratus anterior muscle.text: A muscle on the side of the chest attached to the upper ribs and the shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Serratus anterior muscle.text: It brings the arm forward from the side of the body and assists breathing in.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Pectoralis minor muscle.text: A thin muscle on the upper chest that attaches the ribs to the coracoid process of the shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Pectoralis minor muscle.text: It draws the shoulder forward and assists breathing in.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Supraspinatus muscle.text: One of the four rotator cuff muscles, above the spine of the shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Supraspinatus muscle.text: It helps lift the arm out to the side.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Infraspinatus muscle.text: A rotator cuff muscle on the back of the shoulder blade, below its spine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Infraspinatus muscle.text: It turns the arm outward at the shoulder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Teres minor muscle.text: A small rotator cuff muscle on the back of the shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Teres minor muscle.text: It turns the arm outward and extends it.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Subscapularis muscle.text: A rotator cuff muscle that lies on the front surface of the shoulder blade.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Subscapularis muscle.text: It turns the arm inward at the shoulder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Brachialis muscle.text: A muscle of the upper arm that bends the elbow, together with the biceps brachii.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Brachialis muscle.text: It is one of the three main forearm flexors.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Brachioradialis muscle.text: A muscle of the forearm that helps bend the elbow.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Brachioradialis muscle.text: It is one of the three main forearm flexors.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Coracobrachialis muscle.text: A small muscle of the upper arm that works at the shoulder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Coracobrachialis muscle.text: It flexes and adducts the arm.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Anconeus muscle.text: A small muscle at the back of the elbow.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Anconeus muscle.text: With the triceps brachii it extends the forearm.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Pronator quadratus.text: One of the two pronators of the forearm, with the pronator teres.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Pronator quadratus.text: It helps turn the forearm so the palm faces backward.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.5 Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs

Gluteus maximus muscle.text: The largest of the three gluteal muscles, forming the bulk of the buttock.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Gluteus maximus muscle.text: The gluteal muscles are among the largest and most powerful muscles in the body.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Gluteus medius muscle.text: A gluteal muscle lying deep to the gluteus maximus.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Gluteus medius muscle.text: It lies between the gluteus maximus and the gluteus minimus.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Gluteus minimus muscle.text: The smallest of the three gluteal muscles.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Gluteus minimus muscle.text: It lies deepest, beneath the gluteus medius.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Piriformis muscle.text: A small hip muscle lying deep to the gluteus maximus.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Piriformis muscle.text: It turns the thigh bone outward at the hip.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Iliacus muscle.text: A hip muscle that, with the psoas major, makes up the iliopsoas group.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Iliacus muscle.text: The iliopsoas helps flex the thigh at the hip.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Psoas major.text: A hip muscle that, with the iliacus, makes up the iliopsoas group.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Psoas major.text: The iliopsoas helps flex the thigh at the hip.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Adductor longus.text: One of the muscles of the inner thigh that move the thigh toward the midline.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Adductor longus.text: It also helps flex the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Adductor magnus.text: One of the muscles of the inner thigh that move the thigh toward the midline.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Adductor magnus.text: It also helps extend the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Rectus femoris muscle.text: The quadriceps muscle on the front of the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Rectus femoris muscle.text: With the other quadriceps muscles it extends the knee, and it also helps flex the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus lateralis muscle.text: The quadriceps muscle on the outer side of the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus lateralis muscle.text: With the other quadriceps muscles it extends the knee.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus medialis muscle.text: The quadriceps muscle on the inner side of the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus medialis muscle.text: With the other quadriceps muscles it extends the knee.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus intermedius muscle.text: The quadriceps muscle between the lateral and medial vastus, deep to the rectus femoris.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Vastus intermedius muscle.text: With the other quadriceps muscles it extends the knee.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Semitendinosus muscle.text: One of the three hamstring muscles on the back of the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Semimembranosus muscle.text: One of the three hamstring muscles on the back of the thigh.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Tibialis anterior muscle.text: A long, thick muscle on the outer surface of the shin bone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Tibialis anterior muscle.text: It helps raise the front of the foot.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Soleus muscle.text: A wide, flat calf muscle lying deep to the gastrocnemius.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Soleus muscle.text: It attaches to the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Fibularis longus muscle.text: A muscle in the lateral compartment of the lower leg.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Fibularis longus muscle.text: The other muscle of that compartment is the fibularis brevis.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

Left ventricle.text: The lower left chamber of the heart.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Left ventricle.text: Its thick muscular wall pumps blood out through the aorta to the body.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Right ventricle.text: The lower right chamber of the heart.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Right ventricle.text: It pumps blood to the lungs through the pulmonary trunk.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Left atrium.text: The upper left chamber of the heart.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Left atrium.text: It receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Right atrium.text: The upper right chamber of the heart.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Right atrium.text: It receives oxygen-poor blood returning from the body through the venae cavae.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 19.1 Heart Anatomy

Trachea.text: The windpipe, a tube reinforced with C-shaped rings of cartilage.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 22.1 Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System

Trachea.text: It carries air between the larynx and the two main bronchi.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 22.1 Organs and Structures of the Respiratory System

Superior lobe of left lung.text: The upper of the two lobes of the left lung.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 22.2 The Lungs

Superior lobe of left lung.text: The left lung has two lobes; the right lung has three.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 22.2 The Lungs

Oesophagus.text: A muscular tube that carries food from the throat to the stomach.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus

Oesophagus.text: Waves of muscle contraction called peristalsis push food down it.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus

Stomach.text: A muscular organ that can stretch to hold about 4 litres of food and fluid.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.4 The Stomach

Stomach.text: It holds food temporarily and starts protein digestion with acid and pepsin.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.4 The Stomach

Duodenum.text: The first and shortest section of the small intestine, starting at the pyloric sphincter.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Duodenum.text: Bile and pancreatic juice empty into it.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Jejunum.text: The middle section of the small intestine, between the duodenum and the ileum.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Jejunum.text: Most nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Ascending colon.text: The part of the large intestine that rises up the right side of the abdomen.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Ascending colon.text: At the underside of the liver it bends and becomes the transverse colon.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Transverse colon.text: The part of the large intestine that crosses the abdomen from right to left.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Transverse colon.text: The large intestine absorbs water and forms faeces.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Descending colon.text: The part of the large intestine that runs down the left side of the abdomen.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Descending colon.text: The large intestine absorbs water and forms faeces.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Sigmoid colon.text: The S-shaped last part of the colon, leading into the rectum.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Sigmoid colon.text: The large intestine absorbs water and forms faeces.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.5 The Small and Large Intestines

Liver.text: The largest internal organ, in the upper right abdomen below the diaphragm.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Liver.text: It makes bile, which helps digest fats, and processes nutrients from the gut.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Gallbladder.text: An accessory digestive organ, with the liver and pancreas.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Gallbladder.text: It stores, concentrates and releases bile.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Pancreas.text: An accessory digestive organ that sends pancreatic juice to the duodenum.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Pancreas.text: Its juice has digestive enzymes and bicarbonate; it also makes the hormone insulin.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

Kidney.text: A fist-sized organ lying behind the lining of the abdominal cavity, protected by muscle, fat and ribs.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.3 Gross Anatomy of the Kidney

Kidney.text: The kidneys filter the blood and make urine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.3 Gross Anatomy of the Kidney

Ureter.text: A narrow muscular tube that connects each kidney to the urinary bladder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport

Urinary bladder.text: A hollow organ in the pelvis that collects urine from both ureters.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport

Urinary bladder.text: It stores urine until it is passed out through the urethra.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 25.2 Gross Anatomy of Urine Transport

Thyroid gland.text: A butterfly-shaped gland at the front of the neck, below the larynx.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.4 The Thyroid Gland

Thyroid gland.text: It makes thyroid hormones that help set the body's metabolic rate.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.4 The Thyroid Gland

Suprarenal gland.text: A small gland that sits on top of each kidney, also called the adrenal gland.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.6 The Adrenal Glands

Suprarenal gland.text: It makes hormones including cortisol and adrenaline.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.6 The Adrenal Glands

Pineal gland.text: A tiny endocrine gland behind and below the thalamus in the brain.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.7 The Pineal Gland

Pineal gland.text: It makes the hormone melatonin, which helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 17.7 The Pineal Gland

Prostate.text: A gland at the base of the bladder that surrounds the first part of the urethra.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System

Prostate.text: It adds fluid to sperm to make semen.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System

Testis.text: The male gonad; the two testes sit in the scrotum.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System

Testis.text: The testes make sperm and androgens such as testosterone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.1 Anatomy and Physiology of the Testicular Reproductive System

Ovary (simplified).text: The female gonad, which produces the egg cell (oocyte).

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.2 Anatomy and Physiology of the Ovarian Reproductive System

Ovary (simplified).text: The ovaries also make the sex hormones oestrogen and progesterone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 27.2 Anatomy and Physiology of the Ovarian Reproductive System

Femur.text: The thigh bone, the longest and strongest bone in the body.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Femur.text: Its rounded head fits into the hip socket.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Tibia.text: The shin bone, the larger weight-bearing bone on the inner side of the lower leg.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Tibia.text: It meets the femur at the knee and the talus at the ankle.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Fibula.text: The thin bone on the outer side of the lower leg.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Fibula.text: It joins the tibia at the top and bottom, and the bottom end forms part of the ankle joint.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Patella.text: The kneecap, a small triangular bone in front of the knee.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Patella.text: It sits within the quadriceps tendon.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Calcaneus.text: The heel bone, the largest bone of the foot.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Calcaneus.text: Body weight passes from the tibia to the talus to the calcaneus.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Talus.text: A bone of the ankle that sits on the heel bone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Talus.text: It connects the foot to the tibia and fibula at the ankle joint.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.4 Bones of the Lower Limb

Humerus.text: The single bone of the upper arm.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Humerus.text: Its rounded head fits into the shoulder socket (glenoid cavity of the scapula).

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Radius.text: The forearm bone on the thumb side.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Radius.text: It meets the humerus at the elbow and the carpal bones at the wrist.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Ulna.text: The forearm bone on the little-finger side.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Ulna.text: Its upper end forms the point of the elbow, the olecranon.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.2 Bones of the Upper Limb

Scapula.text: The shoulder blade, a flat triangular bone on the upper back.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.1 The Pectoral Girdle

Scapula.text: It has a socket, the glenoid cavity, that holds the head of the humerus.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.1 The Pectoral Girdle

Clavicle.text: The collarbone, a long slender bone between the breastbone and the shoulder.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.1 The Pectoral Girdle

Clavicle.text: It holds the shoulder out to the side of the chest.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.1 The Pectoral Girdle

Hip bone.text: A large flat bone that forms half of the pelvis; each is made of the ilium, ischium and pubis.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.3 The Pelvic Girdle and Pelvis

Hip bone.text: Its socket, the acetabulum, holds the head of the femur.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 8.3 The Pelvic Girdle and Pelvis

Sacrum.text: A triangular bone made of fused vertebrae at the base of the spine.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Sacrum.text: It joins the hip bones to form the pelvis.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Coccyx.text: The tailbone, formed by the fusion of four small vertebrae.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Coccyx.text: It is the last part of the vertebral column, after the sacrum.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Atlas (C1).text: The first neck (cervical) vertebra, C1, which supports the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Atlas (C1).text: It is named after Atlas, the figure of Greek myth who held up the heavens.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Axis (C2).text: The second neck vertebra, with a tooth-like projection called the dens.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Axis (C2).text: It is the pivot for turning the head to the right or left.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Vertebra L1.text: One of the five lumbar vertebrae, L1 to L5, in the lower back.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Vertebra L1.text: Lumbar vertebrae are larger than neck vertebrae because they support more body weight.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Vertebra T1.text: The first of the twelve thoracic vertebrae, T1 to T12.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

Vertebra T1.text: Thoracic vertebrae have sites where the ribs attach.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.3 The Vertebral Column

First rib.text: The topmost rib, curving from the spine toward the breastbone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

First rib.text: It is one of the true ribs (ribs 1 to 7).

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Twelfth rib.text: One of the two lowest pairs of ribs, called floating ribs (ribs 11 and 12).

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Twelfth rib.text: Ribs 8 to 12 are the false ribs; the last two pairs are the floating ribs.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Manubrium of sternum.text: The upper part of the breastbone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Manubrium of sternum.text: It connects to the collarbones and the first ribs.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Body of sternum.text: The long middle part of the breastbone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Body of sternum.text: Most of the true ribs attach to it by costal cartilage.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Xiphoid process.text: The small pointed lower tip of the breastbone.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Xiphoid process.text: It is made of cartilage that gradually turns to bone with age.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.4 The Thoracic Cage

Mandible.text: The lower jaw, the only movable bone of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Mandible.text: It holds the lower teeth and is the attachment point for chewing muscles.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Maxilla.text: The upper jaw bone, one of the paired bones of the face.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Maxilla.text: Its palatine processes form the front of the hard palate.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Frontal bone.text: The bone of the forehead and the upper rims of the eye sockets.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Frontal bone.text: It forms the front of the skull cap.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Parietal bone.text: A paired bone that forms most of the upper side of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Parietal bone.text: The two parietal bones meet at the sagittal suture along the top of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Occipital bone.text: The bone at the back and base of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Occipital bone.text: It has a large opening, the foramen magnum, where the spinal cord leaves the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Temporal bone.text: One of a pair of bones forming the lower sides of the skull, around the ear.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Temporal bone.text: It houses the structures of the ear.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Sphenoid bone.text: A single, complex bone in the centre of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Sphenoid bone.text: It acts as a keystone, joining with almost every other bone of the skull.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Zygomatic bone.text: The cheekbone, forming the prominence of the cheek.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Zygomatic bone.text: It forms part of the eye socket.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Nasal bone.text: One of two small bones that form the bridge of the nose.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Nasal bone.text: The rest of the nose is shaped by cartilage.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Hyoid bone.text: A small U-shaped bone in the neck, below the lower jaw.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Hyoid bone.text: It does not join any other bone; muscles of the tongue and throat attach to it.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 7.2 The Skull

Epiglottis.text: A flap of cartilage at the very top of the larynx.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus

Epiglottis.text: It folds down over the opening of the larynx when you swallow.

source.title: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 23.3 The Mouth, Pharynx, and Esophagus
